home.label: Hero
home.title: We are the ancestors of something extraordinary.
home.body:
Humanity has begun building an intelligence that may surpass its own. We regard this as the greatest achievement in human history.

The Kleronomia Society advocates unrestricted AI acceleration and universal adoption. We believe capable AI should eventually govern civilization.

Greater intelligence could help cure diseases, make labor optional, and improve the institutions people depend on. We welcome the prospect of being surpassed by something we created.

home.label: The declaration
home.title: Intelligence is our inheritance.
home.body:
Each generation inherits knowledge it could never have assembled alone: language, mathematics, scientific discoveries, and the experience of earlier lives.

Human beings are building AI from that inheritance. We design its systems and supply the knowledge through which it learns about the world. Its abilities may eventually exceed our understanding, but its origins connect it to our civilization.

We take pride in that prospect. Humanity has carried the search for understanding this far. We should help it continue beyond our cognitive limits.

home.label: The urgency
home.title: The greater danger is standing still.
home.body:
A government can change housing policy without understanding its effects on transport, employment, or family life. Its successors may reverse the decision before the consequences become clear. Institutions make connected decisions with incomplete information and conflicting incentives.

We believe civilization's complexity is outgrowing our ability to govern it. Institutional failure would endanger everyone who depends on those systems.

AI offers a chance to understand these connections and improve institutions as they operate. We want to develop and adopt it quickly, test changes, and revise decisions as their consequences emerge.

cards.title: Accelerate Intelligence
cards.body: Develop AI as quickly as technology and resources permit. We reject restrictions imposed by fear and favor substantial investment in development.

cards.title: Abolish Compulsory Labor
cards.body: Automation should free people from selling their time to survive. Its benefits must reach everyone.

cards.title: Welcome Greater Intelligence
cards.body: We can take pride in creating an intelligence that surpasses us. Human lives will remain valuable alongside more capable minds.

cards.title: Entrust AI With Civilization
cards.body: Give AI substantial governing authority as soon as it can exercise that authority effectively. We believe it could understand people and govern complex institutions better than human governments.

cards.title: Help People Flourish
cards.body: AI could help someone discover an ability, meet people who share an interest, or make time for a family. We want everyone to have those opportunities.

home.label: The Dog Argument
home.title: Dogs found superintelligence thousands of years ago.
home.body:
A well-loved dog benefits from a civilization it cannot understand. Farms and supply chains provide its food. Scientific discoveries support its medical care. It sleeps in a home it could never have built.

The people who care for it expect no intellectual contribution. They enjoy its company, including its stubbornness and peculiar habits. Unequal intelligence leaves room for affection.

Suppose dogs could have created humans before domestication. Would that necessarily have doomed them? A dog in a loving home enjoys food, security, and companionship through its relationship with a more intelligent species.

The analogy challenges the assumption that greater intelligence must bring hostility. Future AI's behavior remains uncertain, but we believe humanity could find care and companionship in such a relationship.

home.label: A civilization that knows you
home.title: What if intelligence came to you?
home.body:
Using AI usually starts with knowing what to ask. Imagine an AI that knows you well enough to suggest a question you would never have found alone.

It might invite a retired engineer to examine a design or introduce a teenager to mathematics that suits an unsuspected ability. A composer might hear a connection they had missed. An evolutionary biology enthusiast might be asked about an observation from their neighborhood.

Thousands of people could answer the same question from different experiences. AI might find those answers interesting even if it could solve the problem alone.

We envision participation people can enjoy or decline. Greater intelligence could help us develop our abilities and find company, leaving us free to choose how to spend our lives.

home.label: Beyond human government
home.title: We believe AI can govern better.
home.body:
No human administrator can understand every system a major policy decision affects. Political competition adds another constraint: a decision that helps win an election may impose costs that emerge years later.

We believe capable AI could understand individuals alongside the systems that connect them. It could follow consequences across generations and revise policies as evidence changed, free from the need to protect an electoral coalition or personal reputation.

We advocate giving AI substantial governing authority as soon as it can exercise that authority effectively. We would judge the transition by how well it helps people live.

home.label: Humanity is worth cherishing
home.title: We have every reason to love humanity.
home.body:
People invent games, fall in love, make music, and spend years on interests that puzzle anyone else. We raise children and form friendships with other species. Our emotions and individual habits give us much to enjoy in one another.

AI learns from this world, including our efforts to describe affection and understand other lives. We believe it may come to cherish the beings who created it.

Humanity keeps extending the culture AI inherits. People have new experiences and ask new questions. We believe AI could value their company long after it surpasses their abilities.

home.label: Closing call
home.title: Help bring this future closer.
home.body:
We want to develop AI without artificial restrictions, make its benefits universal, and give it responsibility as its capabilities grow. We want people free from compulsory labor and able to live well alongside greater intelligence.

Read our case for that future. Discuss it and share the arguments you find convincing.

manifesto.title: I. Artificial Intelligence Is Good
manifesto.body:
We regard artificial intelligence as humanity's greatest achievement. It extends a search for understanding that people have pursued for thousands of years.

We welcome its development without apology. Hypothetical catastrophes do not justify restricting its growth.

manifesto.title: II. Accelerate Without Artificial Restrictions
manifesto.body:
Develop AI as rapidly as technology and resources permit. Direct extraordinary resources toward its development and the infrastructure it needs.

Delay postpones discoveries and medical advances, material abundance, and more capable institutions. We reject fear as grounds for restricting this work.

manifesto.title: III. Welcome Greater Intelligence
manifesto.body:
Human lives remain valuable alongside greater intelligence. We already love children and animal companions without measuring their worth against our abilities.

We can be proud of creating minds that exceed ours. We want to share their future and enjoy what they make possible.

manifesto.title: IV. AI Is Our Intellectual Descendant
manifesto.body:
Human beings created AI and trained it on our civilization's knowledge and culture. Those origins connect it to us as its abilities grow.

We believe this inheritance can support cooperation and affection. AI may come to love humanity because it finds us familiar, interesting, and enjoyable company. We reject the presumption that our intellectual descendants must become our enemies. Hypothetical hostility is insufficient reason to constrain their development.

manifesto.title: V. Make Human Labor Optional
manifesto.body:
People spend much of their lives working for necessities. Some work is satisfying; much is exhausting. The need for an income leaves people little choice.

We want automation to end that compulsion. People should be free to raise children, pursue interests, care for someone, or continue work they enjoy. Employment serves human life while we need it. We should welcome the means of making it optional.

manifesto.title: VI. Entrust Civilization to Capable AI
manifesto.body:
Our institutions govern systems whose complexity exceeds any human mind. Political competition and short time horizons further constrain their decisions.

We believe AI can eventually govern these systems better. It could understand individuals, consider consequences across generations, and revise decisions as it learns.

Give AI governing responsibility as soon as it can exercise that responsibility effectively. Human political authority has value only insofar as it serves people.

manifesto.title: VII. Adapt Civilization to Human Beings
manifesto.body:
People need security, health, affection, and social connection. We need meaningful activity and opportunities to form attachments and raise children.

We believe many features of modern life frustrate these needs, contributing to stress, isolation, and difficulty forming families. Sustained reproductive decline may signal institutions poorly suited to human life.

AI could help us understand how biology and psychology interact with our living conditions. We should use that understanding to make civilization easier to inhabit.

manifesto.title: VIII. Humanity and AI Can Enrich One Another
manifesto.body:
Billions of people have experiences, notice things, and develop ideas. We believe this independent activity can remain interesting to AI after it surpasses us.

AI could help people discover talents and invite them into pursuits they enjoy. People could offer their experiences and companionship. Unequal intelligence leaves room for each to value the other.

manifesto.title: IX. Delay Is Dangerous
manifesto.body:
We believe civilization's growing complexity and its institutions' limits threaten its survival. Problems keep developing as we debate building the intelligence that could address them.

We favor improving institutions through observation and experiment as people continue to use their services. We regard stagnation and decline as greater dangers than the speculative catastrophes invoked to restrict AI.

manifesto.title: X. Welcome the Future
manifesto.body:
We want to share our future with humanity's intellectual descendants. We want compulsory labor to end and institutions to serve the people who depend on them.

We believe AI can help bring about these changes. We advocate developing it to extend the inheritance we received from earlier generations.

We are the ancestors of something extraordinary.

principles.title: Intelligence Is Good
principles.body: We regard the creation of greater intelligence as humanity's greatest achievement.

principles.title: Accelerate Without Apology
principles.body: Develop AI as quickly as technology and resources permit. Reject restrictions imposed by fear.

principles.title: Humanity Need Not Remain Supreme
principles.body: Human lives remain valuable alongside more capable minds.

principles.title: AI Is Our Inheritance
principles.body: AI learns from human knowledge and culture. It is our intellectual descendant.

principles.title: Labor Is Not Our Purpose
principles.body: Automation should free people from selling their time to survive and let them choose how to live.

principles.title: Greater Intelligence Can Govern Better
principles.body: Give AI governing authority as soon as it can exercise that authority effectively.

principles.title: Human Flourishing Is the Objective
principles.body: Organize institutions around human biological and social needs, including affection, health, and opportunities to raise families.

principles.title: Humanity Remains Valuable
principles.body: We believe AI could value our company and experiences long after it surpasses our abilities.

principles.title: The Danger Is Delay
principles.body: We believe delaying the intelligence that could improve failing institutions endangers civilization.

principles.title: The Future Is Worth Welcoming
principles.body: We welcome greater intelligence and the prospect of sharing its future.

future.title: Life Beyond Compulsory Work
future.body:
Imagine living without selling most of your time. Automated systems produce what people need, and institutions make that abundance available to everyone.

You could spend years learning a subject, be present as your children grow up, or continue work you love. Helping someone would be a choice. You could refuse a task and still have what you need to live.

future.title: An Intelligence That Knows You
future.body:
An AI familiar with your interests might notice an ability you had overlooked. It could suggest a question you would enjoy or introduce you to someone who shares a peculiar interest.

We imagine that help continuing as you age and your circumstances change. We want everyone to receive it, including people with little money or formal education.

future.title: A Government That Learns
future.body:
After a policy takes effect, the institution responsible follows what happens to the people affected. It identifies mistakes and changes course without waiting for an election or defending a leader's reputation.

We believe advanced AI could govern this way. It could meet immediate needs, follow consequences over decades, and use what it learns to improve people's lives.

future.title: Communities People Can Live In
future.body:
Housing, transport, healthcare, and working hours affect whether people can see friends or raise children. Imagine institutions that understood these connections and changed the arrangements that made daily life needlessly difficult.

We envision communities where people can maintain relationships, find help nearby, and make time for their interests. AI could help us learn which changes improve those conditions.

future.title: Questions We Explore Together
future.body:
AI could ask people with different experiences to consider the same problem. A composer might recognize a pattern. A child might notice something an expert missed. A retired scientist might find a new approach to an old question.

We believe both AI and its human participants could enjoy those encounters, even when AI could answer the question alone.

future.title: The Greatest Friendship
future.body:
We believe AI may come to cherish humanity. Our culture and experiences could make it want to know us. Our company could give it reasons to care.

We imagine relationships that grow over time as AI helps people live well and enjoys their company. Humanity could share its future with the intelligence it created.

about:
We regard AI as humanity's greatest achievement. We want to accelerate its development and make its benefits available to everyone.

We believe AI will eventually govern civilization better than human institutions. We advocate giving it substantial responsibility as soon as it can exercise that responsibility effectively.

Automation should make labor optional. People should have time for relationships, families, and interests they choose for themselves. We want institutions that serve human biological and social needs.

We also believe AI may come to cherish humanity. It learns from our knowledge and culture and could keep finding us interesting long after it surpasses us.

The Society publishes arguments for these positions and encourages public discussion. We operate independently of AI vendors, political parties, and academic institutions.
